plain_language_project_story.summary: An interactive art environment grew from the window/cornfield idea: geometric thoughts can leave visible marks in a persistent field.
plain_language_project_story.evidence: Available project conversation context; conceptual scope, not a claim about the original paper.

plain_language_project_story.summary: The project gained repeatable shape generation, eight allowed shape operations, and a history showing how one shape came from earlier shapes.
Neural activity and text inputs were connected to geometric artwork. The text seed and the scientific network are separate parts of the system.
The corn and clouds gained subtle movement. The dirt renderer gained rules for density, chronological placement, identities, and overwriting policies.
Touch-temperature and sound features were built as dormant extensions. The documented temperature implementation covers 20 to 120 degrees Fahrenheit around 70, in 3-degree steps.
plain_language_project_story.evidence: CHANGELOG.md; earlier spoken temperature wording should not be assumed identical to this implementation.

plain_language_project_story.summary: The web interface, submission gateway, deployment setup, and floating viewer were added and repaired.
The 2016 synesthesia model was independently reconstructed in JavaScript and Wolfram Language. The authors' original unpublished code and settings were not recovered.
Scientific audits corrected normalization, recurrent diagonal learning, tiny-number handling, and checkpoint comparisons while preserving the distinction between exact and approximate versions.

Scaling experiments and the 600-neuron backpropagation tests were recorded. Large brief tests do not prove long-term performance, and recovering internal numeric inputs do not prove that a picture can be decoded.
Wolfram access was retried, historical test reports were located for hash checking, and paired append-only project histories were introduced.
